title: Sudoku Board Check
statement:
You get a 9×9 Sudoku board as a grid of characters. A cell holds a digit "1"–"9" or "." for empty.

Return true if the filled cells break none of the three rules:

  • no digit appears twice in the same row,
  • no digit appears twice in the same column,
  • no digit appears twice in the same 3×3 box (the nine boxes that tile the board without overlapping).

Empty cells are ignored. You do not need to check whether the puzzle can be solved.

examples.why: Every row, column and box holds each digit at most once.

examples.in: the board from example 1 with "4" written at row 0, column 1
examples.why: Row 0 and column 1 have no other 4, but the top-left box already has a 4 at row 2, column 2. Checking only rows and columns would miss it.

examples.in: row 0 is "1" to "8" followed by ".", row 1 has "9" at column 7, every other cell is "."
examples.why: No rule is broken, even though the cell at row 0, column 8 can never be filled. Solvability is not part of the check.

hints: Each of the 27 units (9 rows, 9 columns, 9 boxes) needs its own "seen" set. Which unit does cell (r, c) belong to?
Rows and columns are easy. For boxes, map (r, c) to one box number from 0 to 8 using integer division by 3.
box = 3 · floor(r / 3) + floor(c / 3). One pass over the 81 cells, checking and adding the digit to its row set, column set and box set.

explain.intuition:
The board is just 27 small "no repeats" checks: 9 rows, 9 columns and 9 boxes. Each cell belongs to exactly one of each. So keep a seen-set per unit, visit every filled cell once, and fail as soon as a digit is already in any of its three sets.

The only trick is the box number. floor(r / 3) says which band of rows the cell is in, floor(c / 3) which band of columns. 3 · floor(r / 3) + floor(c / 3) turns that pair into 0–8, like turning (row, column) into a flat index.
steps: Create 9 sets for rows, 9 for columns and 9 for boxes.
Visit every cell (r, c). Skip it if it is ".".
If the digit is already in rows[r], cols[c] or boxes[box], return false. Otherwise add it to all three.
pitfalls: Using floor(r / 3) + floor(c / 3) as the box number: boxes (0, 1) and (1, 0) both get 1, so a 7 at row 0, column 4 and a 7 at row 4, column 0 look like a clash.
Trying to solve the puzzle. Only the filled cells are checked.
Counting the "." cells as repeats of each other.

complexity.time: O(81), constant for a fixed board size

solutions.title: Check rows, columns and boxes separately
solutions.idea: Three rounds of the same job: for each of the 27 units, collect its nine cells and look for a repeated digit.
solutions.time: O(n²) for an n × n board; constant here

solutions.title: One pass with 27 seen-sets
solutions.idea: Visit each filled cell once and test its digit against the set for its row, its column and its box.
solutions.time: O(n²) for an n × n board; constant here

followups: Replace the 27 sets with 27 integers used as bitmasks. What does the check become?
Now fill in the empty cells so the board is solved. Which pattern does that need?
